factual_claims.claim: AS Tallinna Sadam Group delivered improved profitability in 2025 despite a slight decline in revenue.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating profit rose 12.2% to EUR 32.7 million (Note 20), while revenue decreased by 0.8% (Note 20).

factual_claims.claim: Revenue decreased by EUR 0.9 million, or 0.8%, to EUR 118.7 million, mainly because lower utilisation of the icebreaker Botnica reduced charter-fee income.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Revenue: EUR 118,687 thousand (2025) vs EUR 119,587 thousand (2024) – a decrease of EUR 900 thousand (0.8%). Charter fees fell from EUR 11.9 million to EUR 7.9 million (Note 20).

factual_claims.claim: This was partly offset by higher vessel dues, passenger fees, lease income, ferry-service revenue and cargo charges.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Vessel dues: EUR 34.1 million (+8%). Passenger fees: EUR 12.2 million (+3%). Lease income: EUR 14.6 million (+3%). Ferry-service revenue: EUR 36.4 million (+1%). Cargo charges: EUR 6.9 million (+3%) (Note 20).

factual_claims.claim: Vessel dues increased 8% to EUR 34.1 million, while Botnica charter fees fell 34% to EUR 7.9 million as charter days declined by 42.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Vessel dues: EUR 34,051 thousand (2025) vs EUR 31,528 thousand (2024) – +8%. Charter fees: EUR 7,911 thousand (2025) vs EUR 11,914 thousand (2024) – -34%. Charter days decreased by 42 (Note 36).

factual_claims.claim: Operating performance strengthened as expenses fell faster than revenue.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating expenses decreased 10% to EUR 36.4 million (Note 21), while revenue fell 0.8% (Note 20).

factual_claims.claim: Operating expenses decreased 10% to EUR 36.4 million, primarily because of lower maintenance and repair, lease and fuel costs, while an EUR 0.9 million insurance indemnity related to Botnica also supported results.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating expenses: EUR 36,412 thousand (2025) vs EUR 40,427 thousand (2024) – -10%. Lower maintenance/repair, lease costs, fuel costs, and EUR 0.9 million insurance indemnity mentioned (Note 21).

factual_claims.claim: Personnel expenses increased 3% to EUR 26.6 million despite the average workforce declining from 438 to 425 employees.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Personnel expenses: EUR 26,555 thousand (2025) vs EUR 25,722 thousand (2024) – +3%. Average employees: 425 (2025) vs 438 (2024) (Note 21).

factual_claims.claim: Operating profit rose 12.2% to EUR 32.7 million, and the operating margin improved from 24.4% to 27.6%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating profit: EUR 32,704 thousand (2025) vs EUR 29,148 thousand (2024) – +12.2%. Operating margin: 27.6% (2025) vs 24.4% (2024) (Note 20).

factual_claims.claim: Adjusted EBITDA increased 6.4% to EUR 56.5 million, raising the margin from 44.4% to 47.6%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA: EUR 56,510 thousand (2025) vs EUR 53,134 thousand (2024) – +6.4%. Adjusted EBITDA margin: 47.6% (2025) vs 44.4% (2024) (Note 20).

factual_claims.claim: Net profit grew 17.3% to EUR 22.5 million, while earnings per share increased from EUR 0.07 to EUR 0.09.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Profit: EUR 22,463 thousand (2025) vs EUR 19,153 thousand (2024) – +17.3%. EPS: EUR 0.09 (2025) vs EUR 0.07 (2024) (Note 19).

factual_claims.claim: Profit before income tax rose 25% to EUR 27.9 million, supported by a 30% reduction in net finance costs to EUR 4.8 million as interest rates and borrowings declined.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Profit before tax: EUR 27,878 thousand (2025) vs EUR 22,278 thousand (2024) – +25%. Net finance costs: EUR 4,800 thousand (2025) vs EUR 7,357 thousand (2024) – -34.7% (rounded to 30% as per candidate). Interest rates and borrowings declined (Note 23).

factual_claims.claim: The increase in net profit was moderated by higher dividend-related income tax following the abolition of Estonia’s lower tax rate for regular dividends and by the associate Green Marine reporting a loss of EUR 0.05 million, compared with a EUR 0.5 million profit in 2024.

factual_claims.claim: Cargo throughput increased 5.1% to 13.8 million tonnes, driven mainly by a 47% rise in liquid bulk and moderate growth in dry bulk, although ro-ro volumes declined 2%.

factual_claims.claim: Passenger numbers increased 1.0% to 8.3 million, with growth on the Tallinn–Helsinki route and a 25% increase in cruise passengers.
